output.summary: KEP-5607 proposes a new alpha feature gate, UserNamespacesHostNetworkSupport, that relaxes kube-apiserver Pod validation so that Pods may set both hostNetwork: true and hostUsers: false. The KEP is in implementable status at alpha stage.
output.rationale: Control plane components such as kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager run as static Pods with hostNetwork: true, and a validation rule blocks combining that with hostUsers: false. The authors chose a separate gate rather than extending UserNamespacesSupport because that gate is nearing GA and the new behavior depends on external runtime support. Reviewers noted that container runtimes (containerd, runc, CRI-O) need changes before the feature is usable, so alpha is being used for experimentation and to clarify limitations.

alternatives.option: Add the behavior to the existing UserNamespacesSupport feature gate
alternatives.why_not: Rejected because UserNamespacesSupport is approaching GA and adding an immature, externally-dependent behavior would add risk and delay, so the gates are kept separate.

alternatives.option: Do not implement; users use hostPort instead of hostNetwork
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says hostPort may disrupt existing environments, since some privileged containers need direct host network access, and hostPort requires a pre-configured CNI, which static control plane Pods cannot rely on.

evidence.quote: Introduce a new, separate alpha feature gate: `UserNamespacesHostNetworkSupport`. * When this feature gate is enabled, modify the Pod validation logic
Keeping the two feature gates separate is cleaner and safer. Do not implement this feature
crun supports it. I am not sure about CRI-O but I don't see any explicit check to prevent that combination
The Next stage of this KEP must still be ALPHA (e.g. 1.36) and must use NodeDeclaredFeatures library
Since I haven't implemented it in the container runtime and the underlying container runtime yet, I haven't included the implementation details for now.
